Hi Alice — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary of findings below and next steps to reconcile INV-7789.

What we found
- Root cause: During an internal rollout on 2026-08-24 we deployed a change to the sampling-weighting logic used for short-lived streaming sessions. A regression in the rollout logic caused certain reconnect events to be assigned full sampling weight instead of the intended fractional weight. In practice this doubled the billed tokens for sessions that reconnected within 2s of disconnect.
- Evidence: We matched your provided session IDs against our raw sampling snapshots and found ~3,120 affected session events where sampling weight was 1.0 instead of 0.5. See attached log snippets (redwood-usage-sample-log-snippets.csv) with timestamps, session_id, weight_applied, and raw_token_counts.
- Delta estimate: The incorrect weighting resulted in ~1.8M additional billed tokens for ClearSight in Aug, which maps to an overcharge of $12,400 on INV-7789.

What we did
- We rolled back the rollout gate for the sampling change on 2026-08-25 and applied a fix to the weight-assignment logic on 2026-08-26. The fix prevents full-weight assignment on quick reconnects and adds idempotency checks for session attribution.

Proposed remedial action
- Redwood will issue a credit memo for $12,400 against INV-7789. Attached: credit-memo-INV-7789.pdf.
- We will provide a corrected invoice and an accompanying usage export for Aug by EOD Sep 17.
- We'll add your account to the verification cohort for future sampling rollouts (no changes will go to your account without an opt-in test window).

Attachments included:
- redwood-usage-sample-log-snippets.csv (CSV, 900KB) — matched session rows and weight history
- credit-memo-INV-7789.pdf (PDF, 34KB)

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the logs and the remediation steps.

Again, apologies for the disruption — I know this complicates your month-end. Please confirm receipt and whether the proposed credit resolves your finance team's hold.
